title: Five corners of Ibiza
lede: Ibiza is small — you can drive across it in forty minutes — but each corner has its own weather, its own rhythm and its own kind of holiday. These are the five we know best.

regions.name: North
regions.short: Pine woods, stone fincas and the long way round
regions.image_alt: A finca in the pine woods of north Ibiza
regions.title: The north: pine woods, stone fincas and the long way round
intro: The north is the quietest part of Ibiza, and the part that feels most like itself. Roads narrow into pine woods, villages are a handful of whitewashed houses, and the sea appears at the end of a track rather than at the end of a strip.
This is where you come for long lunches in Santa Gertrudis, the Sunday drummers at Benirrás, the hippy market at San Carlos, and coves like Portinatx and Cala San Vicente that reward the drive.

highlights.title: Benirrás at sunset
highlights.text: Drums on the beach on Sunday evenings, and the best sunset on the island's north coast.

highlights.title: Santa Gertrudis
highlights.text: A village square with galleries, coffee and more good restaurants per metre than anywhere else on Ibiza.

highlights.title: Portinatx & Cala San Vicente
highlights.text: Pine-backed coves with clear, calm water — the north's answer to a beach day.

regions.note: The north suits families, walkers and anyone who wants the island at a slower pace. A car is essential; the best coves are at the end of unsignposted lanes.

regions.name: West
regions.short: Sunset coast, salt air and Cala Conta
regions.image_alt: Sunset over a pool on the west coast of Ibiza
regions.title: The west: sunset coast, salt air and Cala Conta
intro: The west has the island's most photographed sunsets, and the beaches that go with them. Cala Bassa, Cala Conta and Cala Salada are a short drive from San Antonio, with water so clear it looks edited.
Inland, the roads climb through almond terraces to Santa Agnès, where the island still feels agricultural. Come in February for the blossom, or in September for the quiet.

highlights.title: Cala Conta
highlights.text: Two beaches, a handful of chiringuitos and a horizon that turns gold at eight.

highlights.title: Cala Bassa
highlights.text: Shallow, family-friendly water and a beach club that has been getting it right for years.

highlights.title: Santa Agnès
highlights.text: Almond groves, a village church and one very good restaurant. The west's best-kept afternoon.

regions.note: The west is the easiest corner for a first visit: close to the airport, close to San Antonio, and pointed straight at the sunset.

regions.name: South West
regions.short: Es Vedrà, Cala Jondal and the good life
regions.image_alt: A turquoise pool and white villa above the south-west coast
regions.title: The south west: Es Vedrà, Cala Jondal and the good life
intro: This is the Ibiza of the postcards: Es Vedrà rising out of the sea, the beach clubs of Cala Jondal, and villas tucked into the hills above Cala Vadella, Es Cubells and Porroig.
It is also where the island's best restaurants cluster — from toes-in-the-sand lunches to long dinners in the hills. You will drive more slowly here, because the views insist on it.

highlights.title: Es Vedrà & Cala d'Hort
highlights.text: The rock, the legend and a plate of seafood at the water's edge. Go early or go at sunset.

highlights.title: Cala Jondal
highlights.text: Beach clubs, boats at anchor and the island's most sociable stretch of pebbles.

highlights.title: Es Cubells
highlights.text: A whitewashed village above the sea, with one of the best views on the island from the church terrace.

regions.note: The south west is where we place guests who want the classic Ibiza holiday: sea views, good food and a short drive to everything.

regions.name: East
regions.short: Promenades, family beaches and the quiet side
regions.image_alt: A lap pool surrounded by pine trees on the east coast
regions.title: The east: promenades, family beaches and the quiet side
intro: Santa Eulària is a proper town rather than a resort: a palm-lined promenade, a marina, and a beach you can walk to from dinner. North and south of it, Cala Llonga, Es Canar and S'Argamassa offer calm water and space for children.
The east gets the morning sun and a little more breeze, which matters in August. It is also where the island's quieter luxury sits — long views, big gardens and not a club in earshot.

highlights.title: Santa Eulària promenade
highlights.text: An evening walk, an ice cream, a table by the water. The most civilised hour of the day.

highlights.title: Cala Llonga
highlights.text: A sheltered bay with shallow water, beach bars and pine shade at the back of the sand.

highlights.title: Es Canar
highlights.text: Home of the Wednesday hippy market, and a good base for boat days up the east coast.

regions.note: The east is our home. Our office is on Carrer Pintors Puget in Santa Eulària, five minutes from the marina — come and say hello.

regions.name: Ibiza Town & Centre
regions.short: Dalt Vila, Talamanca and a short walk home
regions.image_alt: An infinity pool looking across the sea towards Ibiza Town
regions.title: Ibiza Town: Dalt Vila, Talamanca and a short walk home
intro: Dalt Vila is a UNESCO World Heritage site for a reason — a walled town of stone lanes, bougainvillea and sudden views over the harbour. Below it, the marina, the restaurants of La Marina and the boutiques of Vara de Rey.

Stay in Talamanca or Cap Martinet and the beach, the old town and the airport are all within fifteen minutes. It is the most convenient corner of the island, and the one with the most to do after dark.

highlights.title: Dalt Vila
highlights.text: Walk up through the Portal de ses Taules in the late afternoon, when the stone turns pink.

highlights.title: Talamanca
highlights.text: A long curve of sand with a handful of excellent restaurants and the town skyline behind it.

highlights.title: Cap Martinet
highlights.text: Pine-covered cliffs, big sea views and a short drive to both Talamanca and the old town.

regions.note: This is the corner for guests who want to walk to dinner, take a boat from the marina and still be in a private villa by ten.
